title: Oncall Evidence Cookbook: Token Sampling & Artifact Playbook
author: Diane Huang
content:
Summary

Purpose: This cookbook defines the standard evidence, token-sampling methodology, and artifact collection procedures SREs must follow when triaging and reviewing incidents for model inference services (inference-router, model-serving, kv-cache, admission-controller). The goal is to reduce time-to-insight during oncall, ensure reproducible post-incident reviews, and make error-budget/capacity decisions defensible.

Scope and audience
- Applies to: oncall SREs, service owners for inference-router and model-serving, incident commanders, and reliability reviewers.
- Excludes: customer-facing support ticket templates (those live in customer-success).

Key goals
- Standardize minimal evidence that must be captured for any SLO-impacting event.
- Provide token-level sampling, storage, and redaction guidance for telemetry.
- Offer step-by-step runbook actions for triage, containment, and evidence handoff.

Definitions
- Token sample: a compact, redacted snippet of request/response tokens (max 256 tokens) with metadata used for quality or perf regression analysis.
- Evidence artifact: any telemetry, traces, snapshots, or exported memory profiles attached to an incident.
- Burn window: the 1h window we use for immediate error-budget accounting.

Required SLO and error-budget context (examples)
- SLOs (service-level):
  - inference-router latency: P95 <= 200ms (short sequence), P99 <= 400ms.
  - model-serving availability: >= 99.95% (per-tenant).
  - embedding pipeline throughput: 250 req/s sustained per pool.
- Error budget policy: a 3x sustained burn rate over a 1h window triggers a headroom/eviction evaluation; 6x sustained burn in 1h escalates to SRE lead and product oncall.

Minimal evidence checklist (must be collected during oncall triage)
1) Incident header: title, notional start time (UTC), impacted services, oncall names, incident owner.
2) SLO snapshot: P50/P95/P99 and request rate for last 5m, 15m, 1h (attach CSV export).
3) Error budget burn rate and remaining budget per tenant for last 1h and 24h.
4) Representative traces: 5 slow or errored traces with full span data (trace IDs).
5) Token samples: 3 redacted request/response pairs per failing tenant (see redaction rules).
6) Model state: model version, quantization profile, KV-cache hit ratio.
7) Capacity signals: pool utilization, queued requests, GPU mem pressure, preemptions and OOMs.
8) Configuration changes: recent rollouts, autoscaling events, traffic reroutes, and operator commands (gitops commit IDs).
9) Retention: upload artifacts to incident storage and annotate TTL (default 30 days for token samples).

Token sampling & redaction rules
- When to sample: If a request contributes to latency > P95 or a 5xx error, sample it. Additionally, sample 1 in 1000 successful requests per tenant every 10 minutes for regression detection.
- Size limit: samples must be <= 256 tokens (truncate from the tail if needed; keep last tokens that include model output).
- Redaction: remove or replace any content matching PII patterns (emails, phone numbers, SSNs) and customer secrets. Use the redact-service CLI: redact-service --input sample.json --patterns repo:pii --output sample.redacted.json.
- Metadata to attach: timestamp UTC, tenant_id (hashed), route_id, model_version, sequence_length, token_count, latency_ms, trace_id, sample_id.

Token sample JSON (example)
{
  \"sample_id\": \"sample-20260208-az1\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-08T14:12:05Z\",
  \"tenant_hash\": \"sha256:abcd...\",
  \"route_id\": \"chat-completion-v1\",
  \"model_version\": \"redwood-3b-q4\",
  \"sequence_length\": \"512\",
  \"latency_ms\": \"842\",
  \"trace_id\": \"abcd1234efgh\",
  \"input_tokens\": \"<redacted> how do I...\",
  \"output_tokens\": \"<redacted> The recommended approach is...\"
}

Collection procedures (oncall runbook)
1) Immediate triage (0-10 minutes)
   a. Confirm incident ownership and update incident header.
   b. Pull SLO snapshot: run slo-collector query --service inference-router --window 5m,15m,1h --out slo.csv.
   c. If SLOs breached, set severity according to severity matrix and notify PagerDuty channel.
2) Evidence capture (10-30 minutes)
   a. Export top 5 slow traces: traceq top --service model-serving --filter \"latency>p95\" --limit 5 --out traces.json.
   b. Run token sampler: token-sampler sample --filter \"latency>p95 or status>=500\" --limit 50 --redact --out samples/incident-<id>/.
   c. Snapshot capacity: capacity-snapshot --pools inference-gpu-pool-* --out capacity-<id>.json.
3) Containment (30-60 minutes)
   a. If capacity pressure: trigger capacity-orchestrator preempt-protect --pool <pool> --tenants <critical>.
   b. If model regression suspected: rollback model-serving deployment to previous commit: gitops rollback svc/model-serving --to <commit-id>.
   c. If KV-cache corruption suspected: purge kv-cache namespace and warm with synthetic canary (see kv-cache warmup recipe below).
4) Evidence handoff (within 2h)
   a. Push artifacts to incident store: incident-uploader --src traces.json,samples/*,capacity-*.json --incident <id>.
   b. Populate incident ticket with artifact links and tags: add-tags incident <id> slo-breach,token-samples.

Queries and CLI snippets (operational)
- SLO snapshot (Prometheus):
  sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference-router\"}[5m])) by (le) | histogram_quantile(0.95, ...)
- Error budget burn (SQL):
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(error_count) / SUM(request_count) as burn FROM slo_events WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY tenant_id;
- Token sampler (k8s sidecar):
  kubectl logs token-sampler-<pod> -c sampler --since=10m | jq . | gzip > sample-log.gz

KV-cache warmup recipe (when purge occurred)
1) Identify hot tenant routes by rate: SELECT route_id, avg(rate) FROM telemetry WHERE window=10m ORDER BY rate DESC LIMIT 20;
2) Generate synthetic warmups proportional to recent traffic (10% of peak qps per route) with controlled ramp to avoid capacity spikes.
3) Validate hit ratio reaches >= 85% within 15 minutes; if not, increase warmup by 2x.

Priority & escalation matrix (explicit)
- Severity 1 (critical SLO breach, multiple tenants impacted, >6x error budget burn): SRE IC + SRE lead + Product oncall + Exec notify. Immediate mitigation required.
- Severity 2 (single high-value tenant breach or persistent latency > P99): SRE IC + service owner + capacity-orchestrator engaged.
- Severity 3 (low-impact or transient anomalies): Document, collect evidence, schedule post-incident review if recurring.

Post-incident evidence & review standards
- Evidence required for a published postmortem: SLO snapshots pre/post, error budget accounting, at least 3 token samples demonstrating regressions (redacted), capacity snapshots, timeline of operator actions, and a root-cause hypothesis with verification steps.
- Artifact retention: token samples and traces retained 30d; capacity snapshots retained 90d; full heap profiles retained 14d unless requested for longer.
- Naming convention: incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>-<short-desc> for artifact bundles.

Automation & operational tooling recommendations
- Required integrations: token-sampler (sidecar) -> redact-service -> incident-store (S3) with per-tenant ACLs.
- Suggested alerts: composite alert that fires when (P95 latency > SLO AND error_budget_burn_rate > 3) to reduce noise.
- Observability hooks: add structured fields (tenant_hash, route_id, model_version) to all spans for trace correlation.
- Quick-analysis notebook: maintain a Jupyter template that pulls artifacts from incident-store and runs a standard diagnostic pipeline (latency decomposition, model-diff, token-n-gram regression).

Runbook: capacity emergency (playbook condensed)
1) Activate: declare capacity emergency if pool utilization > 95% and queue growth > 3x baseline for 10m.
2) Short-term mitigations (5-20m): ramp down non-critical tenants via priority-evict: capacity-orchestrator evict --selector noncritical --grace 30s --max-evict 25%.
3) Mid-term mitigations (20-60m): shard traffic to spare regions if available, scale up reserved pools (if preapproved), and enable local batching reduction: model-serving config set --batching.enabled=false --route chat-completion-v1.
4) Recovery verification (post-mitigation): confirm sustained P95 latency back under SLO for 30m and error budget burn rate drops below 1.5.

Ownership and contact list
- Oncall SRE: primary responder (PagerDuty).
- Service owner: model-serving@redwood.com.
- Capacity team: infra-capacity@redwood.com.
- SRE lead (evidence review): Evan Brooks.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline template (to paste into ticket)
- 14:12 UTC: Alert fired — inference-router P95 breached (420ms).
- 14:15 UTC: Oncall assigned, SLO snapshot collected (see link).
- 14:20 UTC: Token sampler collected 50 samples; top slow traces exported.
- 14:35 UTC: Autoscaler failed to add nodes (API 5xx), capacity-snapshot attached.
- 14:40 UTC: Rolled back model-serving to commit abc123; latency improved.
- 15:10 UTC: Incident declared resolved; artifacts uploaded.

Appendix B — Auditable evidence checklist (quick table)
- Incident header: YES
- SLO snapshot: YES
- Traces (>=5): YES
- Token samples (>=3 per tenant): YES
- Model version history snapshot: YES
- Capacity snapshot: YES
- Operator commands with commit IDs: YES
